# Snaglist

> A single JavaScript file, with no libraries, that adds a "Report an issue" button to any website or web app.
> People choose the part of the page with a problem and a report type (bug, hard to use, looks wrong,
> accessibility, slow, words, idea), answer its questions, check exactly what will be sent, and send it
> as a GitHub issue, an email, a post to the site's own server, or copy or download it. Reports are anonymous:
> no field contents, cookies, query strings or full browser strings, and emails, long numbers, IP addresses and
> keys are replaced. Each type records the technical details needed to fix it: script errors with stack, console
> errors and warnings, failed and slow requests, steps before, styles and contrast, layout, accessibility details,
> sanitised HTML, Core Web Vitals. MIT licence.

## Install (any site)

1. Download https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheMightyTRex/snaglist/main/snaglist.js into the folder the site
   serves static files from (public/ or static/ in most frameworks). Do not change it.
2. Before </body> in the shared layout: <script src="/snaglist.js"></script>
3. Start once, after the page has loaded (in a framework, in code that runs once, never in a component):
   Snaglist.start({ app: "App name", send: { github: { repo: "owner/name" }, email: { to: "team@example.com" } } });
   Shortest form instead of steps 2 and 3: <script src="/snaglist.js" data-github="owner/name" defer></script>
   Optional: data-types="bug ux visual" to choose the report types.
4. Add data-component="name" to main parts of pages (header, menus, forms, cards, tables, dialogs).
5. Add data-snag-private to anything that shows personal details.
6. Never put a token or password in the page; Snaglist does not need one.

## Settings (all optional)

enabled (true), userToggle (true), launcher ("bottom-right" | "bottom-left" | false), shortcut ("" or
"Alt+Shift+R"), types (["bug", "ux", "visual", "accessibility", "performance", "content", "idea"], or objects
{ id, label, hint, fields: [{ id, label, hint, type: "textarea" | "text" | "select", options, required }],
collect: [parts] }), categories (null | "ux" | "heuristics" | "wcag" | [[value, label, hint]]), severities
("three" | "nielsen" | list), labels (["ux-report"]), collect (each true | false | "auto": page, element,
styles, layout, a11y, html, environment, display, performance, errors, console, network, trail, context),
limits { errors: 5, console: 10, network: 8, trail: 8, slowRequest: 2000 }, page { name: fn, keepParams: [] },
component { attribute: "data-component", from: fn }, context (fn returning app details such as a build
number), redact ([[regex, "[label]"]]),
send { github: { repo, labels }, email: { to, subject }, endpoint: { url, headers }, copy: true,
download: true }, beforeSend (fn(report) => report), text ({ key: "replacement" }).

## Functions

Snaglist.start(settings), Snaglist.destroy({ forget }), Snaglist.open(), Snaglist.report(element),
Snaglist.setUserEnabled(on), Snaglist.isUserEnabled(), Snaglist.redact(text), Snaglist.version.

## User setting (recommended)

A switch labelled "Show Report an issue", on by default, with the hint "A button for telling us about a problem
on any page. Reports never include your personal details." Off calls Snaglist.setUserEnabled(false); on calls
Snaglist.setUserEnabled(true).

## Turn off for everyone

Set enabled: false in Snaglist.start(), or remove the data-github, data-email and data-endpoint attributes.

## Clean removal

Snaglist.destroy() removes its element and listeners and puts back window.fetch, XMLHttpRequest and
console.error and console.warn exactly as they were.

## Remove completely

Delete snaglist.js, its <script> tag, every Snaglist.* call, the user setting and the data-snag-private
attributes. data-component attributes can stay. Search for "snaglist" and "snag-" to confirm nothing is left.
